## Decision and Present Status {.unnumbered}

AffineDrift can explain and test an interchange mapping today, but it cannot define the runtime
`MocapSession` or declare a working C3D export. Those authorities belong to Tools issues
[#4710](https://github.com/D-sorganization/Tools/issues/4710) and
[#4716](https://github.com/D-sorganization/Tools/issues/4716). Neither dependency has a protected,
merged release. The fixtures therefore store `unavailable` with null revision, release, and schema
pins. They are sanitized synthetic **model scenarios**, not captured motion and not C3D binaries.

::: {.callout-warning title="Publication contract, not an exporter"}
This package does not read or write C3D, import a Tools branch, define a competing session schema,
qualify a camera, or establish reader parity. It makes the intended publication mapping and every
known loss executable so that future protected Tools releases can be tested without rewriting the
lesson.
:::

The governed files are:

- [strict publication schema](../schemas/mocap_c3d_publication_compatibility_v1.schema.json)
  and [loss-sidecar schema](../schemas/mocap_c3d_loss_sidecar_v1.schema.json);
- [seven-camera fixture](../data/markerless_mocap/c3d_publication/synthetic_7_camera_v1.json)
  and its digest-bound
  [loss sidecar](../data/markerless_mocap/c3d_publication/synthetic_7_camera_loss_v1.json);
- [eight-camera fixture](../data/markerless_mocap/c3d_publication/synthetic_8_camera_v1.json)
  and its digest-bound
  [overflow sidecar](../data/markerless_mocap/c3d_publication/synthetic_8_camera_loss_v1.json); and
- the deterministic verifier, `scripts/verify_mocap_c3d_publication.py`.

## Vocabulary and Hover Help

<abbr title="A fixed-rate frame of three-dimensional point samples plus its synchronized analog samples">point frame</abbr>,
<abbr title="The nonnegative point reconstruction error; a negative stored residual marks a point invalid">residual</abbr>,
<abbr title="A seven-bit C3D field identifying which of the first seven cameras contributed to a point">contributor mask</abbr>,
and <abbr title="A digest-bound JSON record of semantics that the standard projection cannot carry">loss sidecar</abbr>
have precise meanings here. Confidence is a model score; residual is a geometric error. They are
never treated as interchangeable.

## The Three Records

It helps to separate three layers:

1. The future **canonical session** owns complete camera-independent evidence: frames, clock
   domains, point confidence, contributors, skeleton topology, analog signals, force platforms,
   and processing provenance. Tools owns that contract.
2. A **C3D file** is a terminal interchange representation built around fixed-rate 3D points and
   synchronized analog samples. It has useful, established biomechanics conventions, but it
   cannot carry every modern session semantic in a standard field.
3. The **AffineDrift publication fixture** is a transparent teaching record. It displays canonical
   synthetic inputs, the proposed standard projection, dependency state, and a hashed loss report.
   It owns neither layer 1 nor the conversion implementation.

This separation follows AffineDrift ADR 0001: public pedagogy may project immutable, qualified
evidence, while capture and interchange runtime remain external.

## Frames, Axes, and Units

Each synthetic point is a column vector in an explicitly named right-handed shop frame:

$$
\mathbf{x}_{m} = \begin{bmatrix}x & y & z\end{bmatrix}^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
\mathbf{x}_{mm} = 1000\,\mathbf{x}_{m}.
$$

The source uses metres; the displayed C3D projection uses millimetres. For example,
$[0,0,1.002]$ m becomes $[0,0,1002]$ mm. The verifier recomputes this conversion for every point.
A label or unit declaration alone is insufficient: numeric agreement must also hold.

C3D stores all points against a common coordinate system, but a file does not make an ambiguous
lab frame meaningful. The publication record therefore names handedness and the positive meaning
of each axis. A later Tools adapter must perform any required rigid transform before export:

$$
\mathbf{x}_{W} = \mathbf{R}_{W\leftarrow S}\mathbf{x}_{S}
                  + \mathbf{t}_{W\leftarrow S}.
$$

`W <- S` states the direction; a generic `transform` field would be rejected. These fixtures use
the identity mapping so they teach interchange rather than calibration.

## Fixed-Rate Time and Timestamps

The C3D point sequence is sampled at one `POINT:RATE`, $f_p$. If frame index $k=0$ denotes the
first frame, its relative time is

$$
t_k = t_0 + \frac{k}{f_p}.
$$

At $f_p=200$ Hz, adjacent point frames are $0.005$ s or $5{,}000{,}000$ ns apart. The fixture
contains both indices and integer nanosecond timestamps, and the verifier requires exact agreement
after rounding to nanoseconds. Nonuniform timestamps cannot be represented by merely choosing a
different C3D rate; they require resampling with a declared method or an explicit rejection/loss.

The standard projection retains fixed-rate relative time. It does not claim to preserve the
session's absolute clock origin, clock uncertainty, or device-clock history. That distinction is
recorded as `absolute-timestamp-origin` in each loss sidecar.

The [C3D technical user guide](https://www.c3d.org/docs/C3D_User_Guide.pdf) is the primary format
reference. Its point-frame and event descriptions define elapsed time from the first recorded
frame, rather than a general absolute timestamp system.

## Analog Synchronization

C3D interleaves an integer number of analog sample sets with every point frame. Let $f_a$ be the
common analog sample rate and $n_a$ the number of analog samples per point frame. The required
relationship is

$$
n_a = \frac{f_a}{f_p} \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0},
\qquad
N_a = N_p n_a,
$$

where $N_p$ and $N_a$ are the point-frame and per-channel analog-sample counts. In the fixtures,
$f_a=1000$ Hz, $f_p=200$ Hz, $n_a=5$, and two point frames require ten analog rows. The verifier
rejects a fractional ratio, a mismatched declared ratio, or a sample count other than ten.

All analog channels share one C3D rate. Each channel still has its own label and physical unit.
Repeating `N` or `N*m` across channels is valid and is different from repeating a channel label.
The official [ANALOG:RATE guidance](https://www.c3d.org/HTML/Documents/analograte1.htm) and
[analog-storage description](https://www.c3d.org/HTML/Documents/analogdatastorage.htm) document
the integer-ratio and interleaving rules.

## Residuals, Validity, and Confidence

A point residual is a reconstruction-error quantity. In the EzC3D API, a negative residual marks
an invalid point, commonly associated with occlusion; nonnegative values represent available
residual evidence. The publication verifier enforces the same sign/validity pairing:

$$
r_{k,j} < 0 \Longrightarrow \operatorname{valid}_{k,j}=\text{false}.
$$

The synthetic points are valid and have nonnegative residuals. Model confidence $c_{k,j}\in[0,1]$
is separately bounded. There is no standard C3D confidence field, so confidence remains in the
publication record and the sidecar reports `point-confidence`. Replacing residual by
$1-c_{k,j}$ would invent a calibration relationship and is forbidden.

The [EzC3D project documentation](https://github.com/pyomeca/ezc3d) is used only as primary
adapter/reference evidence at this stage. It documents residual and camera-mask array semantics;
it is not evidence that these JSON examples have passed an EzC3D round trip.

## Seven-camera contributor-mask limit

The standard point contributor mask has seven boolean positions. For contributors among cameras
1 through 7, let $b_i\in\{0,1\}$ indicate contribution from camera $i$. The integer display used by
the fixture is

$$
m = \sum_{i=1}^{7} b_i 2^{i-1},
\qquad 0 \le m \le 127.
$$

Seven contributing cameras produce $m=1+2+4+8+16+32+64=127$. The seven-camera fixture carries
that value for every point and independently preserves the seven camera identities.

An eighth camera has no standard bit. When any contributor lies outside the first seven positions,
the approved provisional policy is:

- set the standard-mask semantic value to `null`/unavailable;
- retain every canonical camera identity in the publication record and sidecar;
- list each overflow identity explicitly;
- bind the sidecar to the fixture by SHA-256 and exact byte count; and
- reject missing, changed, remapped, wrapped, or silently selected subsets.

The eight-camera fixture therefore does **not** publish `127`. That number would falsely claim that
only the first seven cameras supplied the evidence. The complete eight-camera contributors remain
available for a future protected Tools extension or another lossless interchange format.

## Skeletons and Events

C3D point labels can name joints or markers, but point labels do not themselves define a normative
skeleton graph. The fixture maps joint IDs to point labels while keeping directed parent-child
bones in the sidecar. The verifier requires every bone endpoint to be a published joint and every
published point ID to belong to the declared skeleton.

The legacy C3D header provides space for at most 18 event times. Parameters may carry richer event
information in many files, but a publication must not assume all consumers preserve an unlimited
event collection. These fixtures contain one labeled, contextualized synthetic event. The verifier
rejects a fixture with more than 18 events and records the header capacity explicitly. The official
[event-time description](https://www.c3d.org/HTML/Documents/eventtimes2.htm) documents the header
limit and elapsed-time interpretation.

## Force and Analog Data

The examples include six channels—three forces and three moments—and one Type 2 synthetic force
platform. Channel references are zero-based in the publication fixture because this is a software
data structure; a future Tools writer owns conversion to the C3D parameter convention. The
verifier requires:

- one unit entry per channel;
- one value per channel in every analog sample;
- unique, in-range force-platform channel indices;
- exactly four XYZ platform corners; and
- one XYZ platform origin.

The numbers are deliberately simple and are not a calibrated plate trial. Geometry, signs,
calibration matrices, analog scaling, offsets, ADC format, and force-plate type support must be
qualified by Tools M9 and independent readers before a binary can be published.

## Provenance and the Loss Sidecar

A JSON sidecar is useful only when it is cryptographically bound. If $B$ is the exact sidecar byte
sequence, the fixture records

$$
h = \operatorname{SHA256}(B)
$$

and $|B|$, its byte count. Verification reads bytes, checks the length, recomputes $h$, then checks
the sidecar's fixture ID, contributor records, overflow list, and typed losses. Reformatting the
sidecar changes its digest and requires an intentional fixture update.

Every loss has a stable ID, source path, source meaning, C3D meaning, disposition, and explanation.
The baseline losses are absolute timestamp origin, confidence, skeleton topology, and processing
provenance. The eight-camera case adds camera-mask capacity. AffineDrift does not invent a custom
C3D parameter group while Tools M9 is unavailable.

Unknown top-level or nested fields fail closed through exact-key checks and JSON Schema
`additionalProperties: false`. The declared unknown-metadata policy is `reject`. A future Tools
release may instead preserve selected opaque parameters, but that policy must arrive through a
versioned protected contract; it cannot be inferred from this article.

## Compatibility Means Semantic Agreement

C3D writers may choose different parameter ordering, processor encodings, numeric storage, or
padding while representing the same acquisition. Qualification must compare normalized semantic
agreement, not byte identity. The future conformance record should name and pin:

- the protected Tools M1 schema and M9 exchange release;
- the writer and every reader with exact versions;
- the official C3D.org corpus artifact and digest;
- the emitted binary and loss-sidecar digests;
- normalized points, units, rates, residual/validity, masks, events, analog, force-platform, and
  provenance results; and
- every accepted loss before and after write-read-write.

The current fixture records independent-reader qualification as unavailable with empty reader and
corpus lists and a null result. No named reader, sample corpus, byte round trip, or normalized
semantic agreement has run in this slice.

## What the Verifier Proves

The focused verifier proves fixture structure, authority boundaries, primary-source topics,
fixed-rate timestamps, integer analog ratio, point/unit conversion, residual validity,
seven-bit masks, overflow unavailability, skeleton references, force-channel bounds, sidecar
digests, and explicit losses. Its output is a deterministic count summary.

It does not prove JSON Schema equivalence to the eventual Tools schema, binary conformance,
independent-reader acceptance, physical timing, calibration, pose accuracy, privacy review,
render quality, or production readiness. Those omissions are blockers, not implied successes.

## Release Gates

AFF-M3 remains open until all of the following exist:

1. Tools M1 and M9 are protected-merged and immutable releases replace the null pins.
2. Fixtures are adapted through the protected Tools public seam without copied runtime code.
3. Real sanitized C3D binaries pass Tools validation and at least the approved independent readers
   against a digest-pinned corpus.
4. Seven-camera and eight-plus-camera loss behavior is stable across write-read-write.
5. The rendered article receives desktop/mobile, PDF, and Word visual QA under the normal fleet.
6. AffineDrift passes its full protected checks, review, merge, and post-merge verification.

Until then, the package is useful, executable groundwork—and nothing more.
